title: Putting a stream back together
description:
Rebuild the bytes of a TCP conversation from segments that arrived out of order.

```
segments: seq 1006 "World", seq 1000 "Hello ", seq 1006 "World" (again), seq 1011 "!"
stream: "Hello World!"
duplicates ignored: 1, gaps: none
```
hints: After storing a segment, loop: while `m_waiting` has an entry starting at or before `m_next`, take the part beyond `m_next` (lesson 4.04).
A segment that ends before `m_next` is a full duplicate and can be thrown away.
requirements: Start from the initial sequence number; keep out-of-order segments in a `std::map<std::uint32_t, std::string>`.
Append segments as soon as the next expected byte is there; drop duplicates and overlapping parts already delivered.
Report a gap if the stream ends with data missing.
stretch: Handle sequence numbers that wrap past 2^32.
